Backend /api/activity returns HTTP 200 for admin at limit=59, 60, 200, 500 — all 59 records serialize correctly (nested ObjectId in old_value/new_value now coerced via recursive _safe_json). Sales user gets 403 on the endpoint and is redirected on /activity route; nav-activity sidebar link hidden for sales. Frontend /activity page renders full table with 59 rows, columns Timestamp/User/Action/Entity/Details populated correctly (e.g., reassign_lead by Priya Sharma on IRKA07004). No error toast. Sales visiting /activity is redirected to '/' (dashboard) by ProtectedRoute and does not see activity-page container.

issues: Cosmetic Recharts 'width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' console warnings on initial dashboard render — legacy issue from iteration_7, unrelated to this fix.

critical_code_review_comments: _safe_json helper is correctly recursive over dict/list/ObjectId — good defensive fix. Consider using bson.json_util or applying _safe_json globally in a FastAPI response middleware/encoder so future endpoints with nested ObjectId payloads (e.g., mail_history, contact_events with embedded refs) don't hit the same bug.
clean_doc still only converts the top-level _id → id. Nested ObjectIds inside embedded documents rely on _safe_json — worth documenting or merging both into a single serializer.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (admin renders 59 rows, sales blocked as expected)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Activity Log fix fully verified — no regressions. If future ObjectId serialization bugs surface, consider applying _safe_json inside a global response encoder rather than per-endpoint.
rca of the issue: Root cause was legacy activity_log records containing raw bson ObjectIds in nested old_value/new_value dicts (from prior reassign_lead / update_user writes). FastAPI's default JSON encoder cannot serialize ObjectId, so the whole response failed with 500 once such a record fell within the requested limit window (limit>=60 in reproduction). Fix: recursive _safe_json coercer converts all ObjectId → str at any nesting depth (dict/list) applied inside the /api/activity handler at line 1218. Verified across limits 59/60/200/500 → all return HTTP 200 with 59 well-formed records.
